chapter.v:
These were
the names of the sons of Israel (Jacob) who came with him to Egypt along with their families:

Reuben, Simeon,
Levi, and Judah;

Issachar, Zebulun,
and Benjamin;

Dan and
Naphtali, Gad and Asher.

Jacob had
70 descendants there, including Joseph who was already in Egypt.

Eventually Joseph
and all his brothers and all that generation died.

However, the
Israelites had many children and their numbers increased rapidly. In fact there were so many of them that they became very powerful—the country was full of them.
chapter.heading: “A New King . . . Who Didn’t Know Joseph”
chapter.v:
Then a
new king came to power who didn't know anything about Joseph.

He conferred
with his fellow Egyptians and said, “Look at these Israelites—there are more of them than us, and they're more powerful than us.

Let's deal
wisely with them before they become so many that if there's a war they'll side with our enemies and fight us, and flee the country.”

So the
Egyptians made them do forced labor and put taskmasters in charge of them. They used them to build the storage towns of Pithom and Rameses.

But the
more the Israelites were mistreated, the more they grew in numbers and spread out—and the more the Egyptians detested them.

The Egyptians
worked the Israelites brutally,

making their
lives a misery. They made them do hard labor, building with mortar and brick, and all kinds of heavy work in the fields. In all of this hard labor they treated them brutally.

Then the
king gave orders to the Hebrew midwives, Shiphrah and Puah.

He told
them, “When you assist the Hebrew women during childbirth, if you see it's a boy, kill him; but if it's a girl, let her live.”

But because
the midwives revered God, they didn't do what the king of Egypt had ordered. They let the boys live as well.

The king
of Egypt called the midwives in and demanded to know, “Why have you done this— letting the male children live?”

“Hebrew women
aren't like Egyptian women,” the midwives told Pharaoh. “They give birth more easily—they have them before we midwives arrive.”

God treated
the midwives well, and the people increased in number so there were even more of them.

Because the
midwives revered God, he gave them families of their own.

Then Pharaoh
issued this order to all his people: “Throw every Hebrew boy that's born into the Nile, but let every girl live.”
